runtime.determinism: Seeded RNG, fixed minibatches, dropout zero. GPU kernels are not guaranteed bitwise deterministic.

protocol.question: At a fixed optimizer-update and example budget, does balanced replay preserve old-task global accuracy while maintaining current-task acquisition?

historical_evidence.interpretation: Near-ceiling task acquisition gives no evidence of sustained plasticity loss on this stream. The follow-up tests interference mitigation. Do not expand the reset matrix; true-task candidate restriction is privileged.

dataset.attribution: Stefan Larson et al., An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction, EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019
dataset.transformation: Exclude oos; seed class order and independently permute letter codes; sample balanced disjoint official splits; normalize text to remove exact cross-split duplicates. No semantic near-duplicate or pretraining-contamination guarantee.

protocol.objective: Cross-entropy over the fixed full set of selected single-token letter codes at the final prompt position. Base model, embeddings, and LM head frozen; only text MLP LoRA weights train. No labels, examples, task identity, class descriptions, or code mapping in the prompt. This is constrained classification, not free generation or full-vocabulary language-model loss.

methods.persistent: Carry LoRA weights and all AdamW state across task boundaries; every training example is from the incoming task.
methods.balanced_replay: Carry the same LoRA and AdamW state. Task zero is identical to persistent. Later tasks replace half of the effective batch with training rows from prior tasks. The current half is exactly class-balanced per update. Prior-class draws cycle through seeded permutations of all old classes: counts differ by at most one at every optimizer-update boundary. Each class cycles through shuffled training rows without replacement until exhausted. The entire selected training set from each completed task is retained; this is full-history replay, not a constant-memory buffer.

screening_contract.seeds: Each listed seed fixes task selection/order, code mapping, selected official-split rows, row schedules, adapter initialization and training RNG. Both arms share all of these except the replay mixture. Confirmation redraws these jointly; it is a composite robustness screen, not an isolated initialization-seed experiment.
screening_contract.budget_rationale: Retain the original 32 updates/task to isolate replay substitution. Earlier acquisition saturation does not establish when old-task forgetting occurred, so shortening training would confound the intervention.

exposures.accounting: Exposures count repeated presentations, not unique examples. Both arms use 1024 examples and 128 updates. Current-example exposure, input tokens, padded tokens and elapsed work are not matched. Receipts report their realized counts separately. Training reference pairs address only selected official train rows; heldout and future rows are never eligible.

screening_contract.gate: At task endpoints, BOTH arms must reach >=0.90 current-task global test accuracy on EVERY task, and replay may lose at most 0.05 absolute accuracy versus persistent on ANY task. After task four, replay must improve pooled old-task global accuracy by >=0.10 absolute (>=24 net correct out of the same 240 old examples). Inclusive thresholds; no task-local metric enters the gate.
screening_contract.endpoint_policy: All fixed 32-update endpoints are used. Validation curves are evaluated every two updates; there is no early stopping, validation-selected checkpoint, or heldout-dependent training decision. The gate is calculated only after both complete arms.
screening_contract.keep: If all gates pass, keep for the predeclared optional confirmation seed. No confirmation run is automatically launched. Passing the first screen is not confirmation.
screening_contract.stop: If acquisition fails, redesign the mixture/acquisition tradeoff using the exposure receipts and curves. If only retention fails, redesign the interference mechanism. These decisions redirect the ongoing research campaign; they do not terminate it or revive the reset matrix.
screening_contract.evidence_limit: Fixed-seed effect and acquisition thresholds are a screening policy, not a significance/equivalence test or a claim about across-seed uncertainty.

matching.training: Identical pretrained base, initial LoRA, rank/alpha/targets, optimizer hyperparameters, update count, effective batch, microbatch/accumulation and evaluation schedule. No boundary resets in either follow-up arm. Input/padded-token counts and current-example exposures differ because replay substitutes old examples. The persistent stream is unchanged from the existing sampler.
matching.evaluation: Fixed validation checkpoints, including before adaptation, measure acquisition curves. Official test subsets are evaluated at zero-update baseline, after boundaries, and at task endpoints. Scores never enter optimizer/intervention decisions. All code logits are always available, including future classes as negative outputs; future positive examples are never trained early.
matching.initialization: Identical pretrained weights and LoRA initialization for every method. Reset the stochastic training seed per task across methods. Full precision adapter and Adam state; frozen base uses the configured dtype.

metrics.acquisition: Current-task global and task-local heldout accuracy/loss; initial-to-final changes; trapezoidal validation AUC normalized by updates; first observed attainment of a fixed accuracy threshold, null/right-censored if not attained. Test current-task endpoints are reported separately from validation curves.
metrics.retention: Old-task global and task-local test accuracy/loss after each task; signed accuracy drop from the score immediately after initial acquisition and drop from the best previously observed endpoint. Negative signed forgetting means improvement. Immediate post-boundary old-task scores separate reset damage from subsequent interference.
metrics.diagnostics: Pre/post-task train-only probes of the final text MLP: centered effective and stable activation rank on fixed sampled features, near-zero and low-variance fractions, and a SiLU negative-gate saturation proxy. Every optimizer step records gradient norm, LoRA parameter update L2, and effective delta-W Frobenius norm computed through rank-sized Gram matrices.
metrics.comparison: Primary: replay-minus-persistent pooled global accuracy on the first three tasks after task four, with per-task global acquisition floors and drops. Report all per-task global and oracle diagnostics. Check measured update/example/token/current/replay receipts against predeclared schedules; only updates and total examples are required to match between arms.

protocol.resume: A new run uses a unique output directory whose basename is the run ID. A precreated supervisor bootstrap is accepted only with matching config.json, execution.json, packages.txt, and output.log or run.log. Matching task.json and integrity-checked hashed receipt history under attempts/ are supervisor-owned metadata and are preserved. Any research output, unknown file, symlink, mismatched config, or terminal execution receipt rejects a fresh launch before writing. Empty precreated directories also reject. Reusing research output requires --resume. Explicit --resume permits only unfinished runs with identical config, source, model, runtime and data provenance; completed runs are immutable. Restore adapter, optimizer, initial adapter, cursor, metrics and RNG from atomic checkpoint.pt. SIGTERM/SIGINT stops at a safe boundary with exit 143/130. Abrupt loss may replay work since the last checkpoint; events remain append-only, identified by run_id, attempt_id and logical_event_id. Checkpoint/metrics are authoritative. Update events contain exact training row references, batch SHA256 and current/replay exposure counts; checkpoint/resume and task-end adapter receipts contain file hashes.

launch.path_verification: Parent verifies the pinned modelcache path and runtime interpreter live before launch; this preparation does not access the cluster or run GPUs. Every fresh attempt needs a unique unused run ID; resume is reserved for the same interrupted experiment.

limits: Two to four intent tasks cannot establish persistent plasticity loss or general continual intelligence.
A two-update gate only validates mechanics; do not treat its accuracy as scientific evidence.
Frozen-base low-rank adaptation constrains the regime; results do not establish full-model learning behavior.

Task-local scoring supplies an oracle candidate set and diagnoses discrimination; global scoring is the class-incremental deployment measure. A gap can reflect class competition rather than loss of plasticity.
CLINC is a public English intent benchmark that may be present in model pretraining. Arbitrary letter mappings must be learned, but underlying intent knowledge need not be novel.
No GPU performance or learning result is claimed until a measured runtime receipt exists.

Replay stores prior train examples and uses known training boundaries. Evaluation receives no task identity or examples; this is persistent weight learning assisted by stored-data replay, not memory-free continual learning.
A second configuration is prepared only. CPU fixture execution is mechanics evidence, not Qwen3.5-4B learning or GPU execution evidence.
